summary: South Sudan's conservation pledges include a 70% reduction in deforested area by 2030, about 30% of natural forests designated as reserves (against 3% of forest area currently gazetted), and an additional 45.06 million tCO2e sequestered by 2030; the sustainable tourism/recreation sector has a 40% cumulative emissions-reduction target. Restoration includes planting 100 million trees over 10 years and a mixed agricultural-restoration irrigation measure reaching about 20% of farmers in northern Upper Nile. Agriculture targets a 23% cumulative sector emissions reduction and an 18% reduction in soil and livestock-management emissions versus 2017, alongside aquaculture for 10% of farmers, beekeeping reaching 3,000, 5,000 and 6,000 farmers in three regions, and rangeland/water management for 20,000 farmer households. The mixed water plan builds at least 10 structures and boreholes per state. Mapped forest covers 257,287 km² (40.6%), shrubland 44.7%, and agriculture 28,587 km² (4.5%); tree density is unspecified.
